completion_conditions: A `needs_guardian` or `blocked` CCA verdict never produces a repair dispatch, and never consumes a repair attempt.
An unresolvable CCA verdict never produces a repair dispatch and stops with its own reason.
`repair_required` and `insufficient_evidence` still dispatch repairs exactly as today.
Every loop action that appends to `ledger_evidence` after the PR exists also pushes those records to the task branch.
The full suite, the goal-loop, loop-e2e, governance-evidence and adversarial suites and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: DEFECT A — the loop never reads the CCA verdict's VALUE. Measured: `grep -c needs_guardian scripts/shiki_loop.py` returns 0. `decide_task_action` reads only check CONCLUSIONS. It carefully holds POLICY_GATE apart from repairable checks, with a comment citing ADR 0010 — 'an autonomous runner is never told to make the Guardian gate pass'. But a `needs_guardian` CCA verdict surfaces as a red `CCA verdict` check, which lands in `repairable_failed`; once `cca_reruns >= MAX_CCA_RERUNS` the branch falls through to `dispatch_repair`. The same impersonation pathway the POLICY_GATE guard closes is open through the other door.

Measured harm on PR #240: three repair packets (RP-…13b1dd8d, RP-…81c3cedd, RP-…cb805463) and three runner sessions were dispatched against a `needs_guardian` verdict. `git diff` of scripts/ and tests/ between the first head and the last: ZERO files. The packets said `failing_checklist_items: ['required check failed: CCA verdict']` and `minimal_required_changes: ['Fix the failing required checks without broadening scope.']` — an instruction whose shortest satisfying action is to manufacture approval evidence. AGENTS.md and CCA-12 forbid an implementer from doing that; the loop must not issue the instruction in the first place.
Second harm: the default repair limit is 3, so a gate no repair can satisfy CONSUMES the whole budget. A task that later needs a real repair has none left.

The fix is to read the verdict value from durable CI evidence, not to guess from the check colour. The CCA workflow uploads `.shiki/gha` as the artifact `shiki-cca-evidence` (`.github/workflows/shiki-cca-completion.yml` line 436-439), which contains `cca-verdict.json`. `needs_guardian` and `blocked` are never repairable. `repair_required` and `insufficient_evidence` are exactly the verdicts that mean 'the implementer should act', so they keep dispatching repairs.

When the verdict value cannot be resolved — no artifact, unreadable, or the CCA crashed before producing one — the loop must NOT dispatch a repair and must stop with a distinct reason. Fail-closed is right here for two independent reasons: an unresolvable verdict may be a Guardian stop, and a CCA that crashed before judging (`error_max_structured_output_retries`, observed on PR #240) is not something an implementer can repair either.

DEFECT B — the loop appends ledger ids to the task file after the PR exists and never pushes the records. `_sync_state_to_branch` (scripts/shiki_loop.py:716) exists and does exactly the right thing: it commits the task file, the worktree record, and every file referenced by `task.ledger_evidence`, including the transitive `.shiki`-relative evidence each ledger cites. Measured: it is called from exactly ONE place, line 1410, inside the `create_pr` action. The `rerun_cca` and `dispatch_repair` actions both append to `ledger_evidence` in the coordinator mirror and neither calls it.

Measured harm: PR #239 blocked on 3 missing ledger entries, PR #240 on 5, each with `Task ledger evidence L-… is missing at /home/runner/…`. Because the fix requires a push, and a push moves the head, and `guardian_comment.require_head_sha` is true, EVERY occurrence costs a fresh operator approval. Of the five approvals PR #239 and #240 consumed, four were caused by these two defects.

The two are one task. Both live in `scripts/shiki_loop.py` and would serialise on that lock anyway, and separating them would mean two PRs each re-proving the same loop fixtures. The acceptance checks cover them independently so a partial fix cannot pass.
grill_with_docs.source: Measured 2026-08-01 on PRs #239 and #240 against main at cf23117.

non_goals: Changing what `repair_required` or `insufficient_evidence` verdicts do — those still dispatch repairs.
Changing the POLICY_GATE handling, which is already correct.
Changing the repair attempt limit, the CCA rerun limit, or the closeout path.
Changing what MergeGate requires of a branch.
Making the loop merge, approve, or author any approval record.
Touching any file outside the declared locks.
outcome: The goal loop never hands an implementation runtime a repair packet whose only failing item is a judge saying a human must approve, and it never leaves the task branch citing ledger evidence it did not push. Both were measured live on 2026-08-01 while landing the first two remediation PRs: together they turned two correct implementations into five operator approvals and four wasted repair dispatches.

spec_freeze.source: Operator instruction 2026-08-01 to fix every open finding and auto-fix newly discovered ones; both defects were measured live during that work and the operator agreed to fix them before continuing the remaining backlog.

acceptance_checks: A needs_guardian CCA verdict yields stop_guardian, never a repair dispatch, and leaves the repair-attempt counter unchanged.
A blocked CCA verdict yields stop_blocked, never a repair dispatch, and leaves the repair-attempt counter unchanged.
repair_required still dispatches a repair and still increments the attempt counter — unchanged from today.
insufficient_evidence still dispatches a repair — unchanged from today.
A complete verdict against a red check stops with a distinct reason instead of repairing.
An unresolvable verdict (missing, unreadable, malformed artifact, or a CCA that crashed before writing one) never dispatches a repair and stops with its own distinct reason.
Resolving the verdict is read-only and an error resolving it is the unresolvable case, never a loop crash.
POLICY_GATE handling is unchanged — asserted directly.
After a rerun_cca action, every id in task.ledger_evidence resolves to a file present on the task branch, including the transitive .shiki evidence those ledgers cite.
After a dispatch_repair action, the same holds.
_sync_state_to_branch's selection logic is unchanged; only its call sites changed.
scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh covers a needs_guardian verdict producing a Guardian stop rather than a repair.
scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh asserts no emittable repair packet names the CCA verdict check as its only failing item.
tests/test_loop_verdict_gating.py drives the real decide_task_action and effectors for every case above.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.

Changing the repair attempt limit, the CCA rerun limit, or the closeout path

tasks.scope:
DEFECT A — verdict-aware repair gating. `decide_task_action` in `scripts/shiki_loop.py` currently decides from check conclusions alone. When the `CCA verdict` check is red, the loop must resolve the verdict's VALUE from durable CI evidence — the `shiki-cca-evidence` artifact the CCA workflow uploads from `.shiki/gha`, which contains `cca-verdict.json` — and branch on it:
  - `needs_guardian` -> `stop_guardian`, with a reason naming the verdict. Never a repair, and it must NOT consume a repair attempt.
  - `blocked` -> `stop_blocked`, with a reason naming the verdict. Never a repair, and it must NOT consume a repair attempt.
  - `repair_required` or `insufficient_evidence` -> unchanged behaviour: dispatch a repair exactly as today, including the existing rerun-then-repair sequencing and the attempt limit.
  - `complete` with a red check -> the check and the verdict disagree; stop with a distinct reason rather than repairing.
  - value unresolvable (no artifact, unreadable, malformed, or the CCA crashed before writing one) -> NEVER dispatch a repair; stop with a distinct reason that says the verdict could not be read. Fail-closed, because an unresolvable verdict may be a Guardian stop and because a CCA that crashed before judging is not repairable by an implementer either.
Resolution must be read-only and must not fail the loop when the network or `gh` is unavailable — an error resolving the verdict is the unresolvable case, not a crash. Keep the existing POLICY_GATE handling exactly as it is; this change must not alter it.

DEFECT B — push the evidence the task cites. `_sync_state_to_branch` (line 716) already commits the task file, the worktree record, and every file referenced by `task.ledger_evidence` including the transitive `.shiki`-relative evidence each ledger cites. It is called from exactly one place: line 1410, in the `create_pr` action. Every OTHER loop action that appends to `ledger_evidence` after the PR exists — `rerun_cca` and `dispatch_repair` at minimum — must call it too, after its own ledger append, so the branch never cites a record it does not carry. Do not broaden what `_sync_state_to_branch` selects; the defect is where it is called, not what it copies.

Add `tests/test_loop_verdict_gating.py` driving the real `decide_task_action` and the real effectors against fixtures, one case per branch: each of the five verdict values above; the unresolvable case; an assertion that `needs_guardian` and `blocked` leave the repair-attempt counter UNCHANGED; an assertion that `repair_required` still dispatches and still increments; and an assertion that POLICY_GATE handling is byte-for-byte unchanged. For DEFECT B, assert that after a `rerun_cca` action and after a `dispatch_repair` action, every id in `task.ledger_evidence` resolves to a file present in the task branch's worktree, and that the transitive evidence each of those ledgers cites resolves too. Add a goal-loop case in `scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh` covering a needs_guardian verdict producing a Guardian stop rather than a repair, and an adversarial case in `scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh` asserting that no repair packet the loop can emit ever names the CCA verdict check as its only failing item.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  DEFECT A symptom: a high-risk PR whose implementation is correct and whose CCA said 'a human must approve' is handed to an implementation runtime with the instruction 'Fix the failing required checks without broadening scope.' The runner has nothing to fix; the shortest action that would satisfy the literal instruction is to manufacture approval evidence.
  Measured on PR #240 (2026-08-01): three repair packets — RP-20260801T073709042417Z-13b1dd8d, RP-20260801T074031312915Z-81c3cedd, RP-20260801T075241290749Z-cb805463 — and three runner sessions, against `git diff --name-only <first head> <last head> -- scripts/ tests/` = ZERO files. The emitted packet contained `failing_checklist_items: ['required check failed: CCA verdict']` and no acceptance criteria.
  Root cause: `grep -c needs_guardian scripts/shiki_loop.py` = 0. The loop reads check conclusions only. `repairable_failed` strips POLICY_GATE — with a comment citing ADR 0010 and the phrase 'an autonomous runner is never told to make the Guardian gate pass' — but the `CCA verdict` check is not stripped, so a `needs_guardian` verdict reaches `dispatch_repair` once the rerun budget is spent.
  Second harm, measured: the 3-attempt repair budget is consumed by a gate no repair can satisfy, leaving none for a real failure.
  DEFECT B symptom: `MergeGate metadata check` blocks with `Task ledger evidence L-… is missing at /home/runner/work/shiki/shiki/.shiki/ledger/L-….json`. Measured: 3 missing entries on PR #239, 5 on PR #240.
  Root cause: `_sync_state_to_branch` is called from exactly one place — line 1410, the `create_pr` action. `rerun_cca` and `dispatch_repair` append to `ledger_evidence` in the COORDINATOR mirror and never sync. `_commit_and_push_implementation` runs `git add -A` in the worktree, which cannot help: the records were written to the coordinator's `.shiki`, not the worktree's.
  Why they compound: fixing a stranded-evidence block requires a push, a push moves the head, and `guardian_comment.require_head_sha` is true — so every occurrence costs a fresh operator approval. Four of the five approvals PRs #239 and #240 consumed were caused by these two defects, not by any decision anyone needed to make.
  Reproducible when: a needs_guardian verdict yields a Guardian stop with the repair counter untouched, and after any post-PR loop action every id in `ledger_evidence` resolves to a file on the task branch.
